newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan paperboard merger may spur others - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Japan paperboard merger may spur others - analysts.

text.p: Japan's leading paperboard maker, Japan Paper Industry Co Ltd said on Friday it may merge with another paperboard producer, a move which analysts called an attempt to survive increasingly tough competition.
The merger, aimed at cutting costs by streamlining of manufacturing and supply channels, could trigger an overhaul of the nation's crowded paper industry, analysts said.
"The possible merger may prompt a reorganisation of Japan's paperboard industry which is ailing from excessive competition," said Takato Watabe, an analyst at Daiwa Institute of Research said.
Japan Paper, a subsidiary of top paper maker Nippon Paper Industries Co Ltd said it may merge with Jujo Paper Board Co Ltd, another Nippon Paper group company.

Japan Paper said in a statement that the company was considering the merger on condition that it would be able to remain listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange after the merger and win the necessary government approval.
"At the moment, no decision has yet been made," it said, adding that it could not comment further. Media reports said the merger will be finalised in October.
Daiwa's Watabe said that the paperboard business has a lower margin than other paper sectors because there were too many small companies competing for their share in the market.
He added that about 90 manufacturers currently compete for market share.
If consummated, the merged company would become the second-largest paperboard producer after Oji Paper Co Ltd .
Although Nippon Paper may cut costs and streamline its paperboard business through the merger of its two affiliates, the effects on its bottom line may not be as dramatic as it hopes, analysts said.
The parent company is likely to see only some 500 million yen ($4.09 million) to 600 million yen ($4.91 million) added to its group earnings from the merger, Daiwa's Watabe said.

The financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Friday that total annual sales of the merged firm are expected to top 100 billion yen ($819 million), while paperboard output is seen rising to around 1.5 million tonnes per year.
The total output of paperboard in Japan is about 12 million tonnes, and worth about 700 billion yen ($5.73 billion), according to the Japan Paper Association.

The merger news comes only a week after video-game giant Sega Enterprises Ltd announced that it would buy toymaker Bandai Co Ltd to build what they called "a formidable force" in the competitive media entertainment business.
On Friday, The Tokyo Stock Exchange suspended trade in Japan Paper shares for a full day because of pending news on the merger.
Shares in Nippon Paper ended the Friday's session up 21 yen to 543 yen, buoyed by anticipation of the merger. ($1=122 yen)
